outline: 68 Projectile Motion and Velocity as a Vector
190 Deriving the Six Equations of Motion

examples.question_text: A ball is projected from the origin at $28\text{ m/s}$ at $30^{\circ}$ above the horizontal. Take $g=10\text{ m/s}^{2}$. By integrating, derive the six equations of motion and write the velocity and position in vector form.
examples.solution_text:
Take right and up as positive. The initial velocity components are
$\begin{align*}\dot{x}(0)&=28\cos30^{\circ}=14\sqrt{3}\\\dot{y}(0)&=28\sin30^{\circ}=14.\end{align*}$

The acceleration components are $\ddot{x}=0$ and $\ddot{y}=-10$.

Integrate the horizontal acceleration:
$\begin{align*}\dot{x}&=\int0\,dt=C_{1}\\\dot{x}(0)&=C_{1}=14\sqrt{3}\\\dot{x}(t)&=14\sqrt{3}.\end{align*}$

Integrate the vertical acceleration:
$\begin{align*}\dot{y}&=\int-10\,dt=-10t+C_{2}\\14&=-10(0)+C_{2}\\C_{2}&=14\\\dot{y}(t)&=14-10t.\end{align*}$

Integrate again and use $x(0)=y(0)=0$:
$\begin{align*}x&=\int14\sqrt{3}\,dt=14\sqrt{3}t+C_{3}\\0&=14\sqrt{3}(0)+C_{3}\\C_{3}&=0\\x(t)&=14\sqrt{3}t.\end{align*}$
$\begin{align*}y&=\int(14-10t)\,dt=14t-5t^{2}+C_{4}\\0&=14(0)-5(0)^{2}+C_{4}\\C_{4}&=0\\y(t)&=14t-5t^{2}.\end{align*}$

The six equations are
$\begin{align*}\ddot{x}&=0,&\ddot{y}&=-10,\\\dot{x}&=14\sqrt{3},&\dot{y}&=14-10t,\\x&=14\sqrt{3}t,&y&=14t-5t^{2}.\end{align*}$

In vector form,
$\begin{align*}\underset{\sim}{a}(t)&=-10\underset{\sim}{j}\\\underset{\sim}{v}(t)&=14\sqrt{3}\underset{\sim}{i}+(14-10t)\underset{\sim}{j}\\\underset{\sim}{r}(t)&=14\sqrt{3}t\underset{\sim}{i}+(14t-5t^{2})\underset{\sim}{j}.\end{align*}$

examples.question_text: A stone is projected at $18\text{ m/s}$ at $30^{\circ}$ below the horizontal. Take right and up as positive and $g=9.8\text{ m/s}^{2}$. By integrating the acceleration, find its velocity vector at time $t$.
A projectile starts at the origin with velocity $\underset{\sim}{v}(t)=13\underset{\sim}{i}+(16-10t)\underset{\sim}{j}$ metres per second. Find its position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)$.
examples.solution_text:
Integrate each component:
$\begin{align*}x&=\int13\,dt=13t+C_{1}\\y&=\int(16-10t)\,dt=16t-5t^{2}+C_{2}.\end{align*}$

The projectile starts at the origin, so $x(0)=0$ and $y(0)=0$:
$\begin{align*}0&=13(0)+C_{1}\\C_{1}&=0\\0&=16(0)-5(0)^{2}+C_{2}\\C_{2}&=0.\end{align*}$

Hence,
$\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=13t\underset{\sim}{i}+(16t-5t^{2})\underset{\sim}{j}\text{ m}$.

examples.question_text: A ball is thrown from a platform $18\text{ m}$ above the ground at $45\text{ m/s}$ at an angle $\theta$ above the horizontal, where $\tan\theta=\dfrac{4}{3}$. Take $g=10\text{ m/s}^{2}$ and the origin at ground level directly below launch. By integrating, find its velocity and position vectors.

A projectile has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=15t\underset{\sim}{i}+(20t-4.9t^{2}+8)\underset{\sim}{j}$ metres, with $y$ measured from the ground. Find its launch speed and angle above the horizontal, giving the angle to $1$ decimal place.
examples.solution_text:
Differentiate the position vector:
$\underset{\sim}{v}(t)=15\underset{\sim}{i}+(20-9.8t)\underset{\sim}{j}$.

At launch,
$\underset{\sim}{v}(0)=15\underset{\sim}{i}+20\underset{\sim}{j}$.

Use the initial components to find the speed:
$\begin{align*}V&=\sqrt{15^{2}+20^{2}}\\&=\sqrt{625}\\&=25\text{ m/s}.\end{align*}$

Both components are positive, so the direction is above the horizontal:
$\begin{align*}\alpha&=\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{20}{15}\right)\\&\approx53.1^{\circ}.\end{align*}$

The launch velocity is $25\text{ m/s}$ at $53.1^{\circ}$ above the horizontal.

examples.question_text: A projectile starts at the origin with speed $U$ at angle $\beta$ above the horizontal. Its acceleration is $\underset{\sim}{a}=-g\underset{\sim}{j}$, where $g>0$. Integrate twice and use the initial conditions to derive its velocity and position vectors.
examples.solution_text:
Integrating the acceleration gives
$\underset{\sim}{v}=C_{1}\underset{\sim}{i}+(-gt+C_{2})\underset{\sim}{j}$.

Use the initial velocity:
$\begin{align*}\underset{\sim}{v}(0)&=U\cos\beta\,\underset{\sim}{i}+U\sin\beta\,\underset{\sim}{j}\\C_{1}&=U\cos\beta\\C_{2}&=U\sin\beta.\end{align*}$

Therefore,
$\underset{\sim}{v}(t)=U\cos\beta\,\underset{\sim}{i}+(U\sin\beta-gt)\underset{\sim}{j}$.

Integrating again gives
$\underset{\sim}{r}=(Ut\cos\beta+C_{3})\underset{\sim}{i}+\left(Ut\sin\beta-\dfrac{1}{2}gt^{2}+C_{4}\right)\underset{\sim}{j}$.

The launch point is the origin, so $\underset{\sim}{r}(0)=\underset{\sim}{0}$. Thus $C_{3}=0$ and $C_{4}=0$, giving
$\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=Ut\cos\beta\,\underset{\sim}{i}+\left(Ut\sin\beta-\dfrac{1}{2}gt^{2}\right)\underset{\sim}{j}$.

examples.derivation: 28cos30°=14√3 and 28sin30°=14. Integrating acceleration gives ẋ=C1 and ẏ=−10t+C2; the initial velocity gives C1=14√3 and C2=14. Integrating again and applying the origin gives C3=C4=0, hence x=14√3t and y=14t−5t². The six scalar equations and all three vector equations agree. This follows source lines 452–501.

The initial components are 18cos30°=9√3 and −18sin30°=−9. Integrating (0,−9.8) and applying these components gives v(t)=9√3i−(9+9.8t)j. The diagram has a rightward horizontal component, downward vertical component and resultant 30° below horizontal; its component lengths have ratio √3:1. Derived annotations appear only in the solution. The method matches source lines 160–168 and 1406–1417.

Integrating the supplied velocity gives x=13t+C1 and y=16t−5t²+C2. The origin condition makes both constants zero, giving r(t)=13ti+(16t−5t²)j metres. Differentiation recovers the supplied velocity. This matches the vector displacement integration in source lines 388–415.

For the acute launch angle, cosθ=3/5 and sinθ=4/5, so the initial components are 27 and 36. Integrating acceleration gives v(t)=27i+(36−10t)j. Integrating velocity and applying r(0)=18j gives r(t)=27ti+(36t−5t²+18)j. The diagram places the launch above the ground-level origin and shows an upward launch vector with slope 4/3. Its height and coordinate annotations agree with the chosen origin. This follows source lines 1237–1316.

Differentiation gives v(t)=15i+(20−9.8t)j, so v(0)=15i+20j. The launch speed is √(225+400)=25 m/s and the angle is arctan(20/15)=53.1301…°, or 53.1° above horizontal. The constant launch height does not contribute to velocity. This follows source lines 898–911.

Integrating −gj gives C1i+(−gt+C2)j. The initial velocity fixes C1=Ucosβ and C2=Usinβ. A second integration gives (Utcosβ+C3)i+(Utsinβ−gt²/2+C4)j; the origin fixes C3=C4=0. Both resulting vectors satisfy the initial conditions and differentiate to the preceding vector. This matches source lines 560–592 and the general-gravity equations at lines 279–304.
